title: Dock a laptop: lift it level by both sides onto its docking station, then press it down until it clicks
context: Computer user support specialists (O*NET 15-1232.00) set up equipment for employee use, which includes docking laptops at desks. Dell's E-Port docking station guide gives the procedure: "Center the laptop with the E-Port, then push down on the laptop until it clicks" into the docking connector; it also warns not to pick the laptop up while it is docked. The instruction only says to dock the laptop. A closed 13-inch laptop is 31 cm wide, more than three times as wide as a gripper opens, and has no handle, so it is lifted by both sides together and kept level and square while it is lowered, or its socket misses the connector. Lifted by one side, it tips about the other; the docking station stands 1 cm higher than the laptop's stand, so it cannot be pushed across onto it. Its own weight does not engage the latches: both sides are pressed down until both latches click.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left. Laptop (loose, 1.3 kg): a closed 13-inch business laptop, 21.5 cm deep x 31 cm wide x 1.9 cm thick, lying flat on the stand with its middle at x 12, y 0 and its back (hinge) edge toward the docking station; in its underside, centred 3.25 cm in front of its back edge, a 2.2 x 5 cm docking socket, 1.2 cm deep, with a latch slot on each side of it (at y -6.5 and 6.5). Laptop stand (fixed, wood): x 2 to 22, y -10 to 10, 3 cm tall; the laptop's sides overhang it by 5.5 cm. Docking station (fixed, black): x 23.75 to 38.5, y -10.5 to 10.5, its top 4 cm above the table; two guide posts at its back corners (y 7.5 to 10.5 each side, 1.5 cm tall, front faces at x 37.3); the docking connector, 1.6 x 4.4 cm and 0.7 cm tall, at x 33.2 to 34.8, y -2.2 to 2.2; a spring latch hook on each side of it, at y -6.5 and 6.5. Docked, the laptop's middle is at x 26.5 and its back edge rests against the guide posts. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: The bodies' poses are read from the simulation, and each gripper's centre from the arm's joints. 0 for the rest of the run once the laptop has been dropped (its middle falling faster than 0.6 m/s, as from about 2 cm), turned over, knocked off the table, or pulled off the docking station after it clicked in (its socket's mouth 3 mm or more above the connector's base after both latches clicked). Otherwise partial credit is the best stage reached: 0.25 lifted clear of the stand (its lowest corner 1.5 cm or more above the stand's top, tilted under 10 degrees); 0.5 put down on the docking station against the guide posts and let go (its back edge within 5 mm of both posts, its middle within 1 cm of the station's centre line, the middle of its underside within 1 cm above the station's top, tilted under 6 degrees, at rest, both grippers 6 cm or more from it); 0.75 docked (within 3 mm of its docked place, its socket's mouth within 1.5 mm of the connector's base, level within 2 degrees, both latch hooks back over their catches). 1.0: docked, both grippers 6 cm or more from the laptop, still for 1 s. Doing nothing scores 0. On a real dock, docked means it clicked, sits flush and level against the guide posts and the dock's docking light is on; the rest is measured with a ruler and a protractor from the overhead and wrist videos.
reset_notes: Undock the laptop (press the docking station's eject button) and lay it back on the stand as in the screenshot. In the simulation each trial starts the simulator afresh (each inspect-robots run does).
fidelity: Rigid bodies in Isaac Sim 6.1 (PhysX), 20 Hz control. The laptop is one rigid block with its socket and two latch slots; the docking station is a fixed block with two guide posts, a plain connector block (no contacts) and two latch hooks, each a steel nose on a 5000 N/m spring slide. Electrical docking is not modelled. The laptop's front overhangs the station by 8 cm instead of resting on the desk in front of it. The stand is a plain block.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both arms came to the laptop's left and right sides near its back corners and stayed there; the laptop was never lifted off its stand); demo: 1.0
